cards.text: The Teacher, son of David and king in Jerusalem, has just asked who knows what is good for a man in his few, fleeting days that pass like a shadow (Eccl 1:1; 6:12). Now he lays out a string of things that are better than other things. First up: a good name is better than fine perfume.

cards.question: Right after the perfume line, the Teacher compares two days in a person's life. True or false: he says a person's day of birth is better than his day of death.

cards.text: Then he says it's better to enter a house of mourning than a house of feasting. Friend, the man is walking PAST the party to get to the house where everybody's crying, and he's doing it ON PURPOSE.

cards.question: Why does the Teacher say the house of mourning is the better place to go?

cards.text: Next he says sorrow is better than laughter, for a sad countenance is good for the heart. Friend, that's a tough line for a stamper who can't stop laughing, because I'm reading it with a straight face and my mustache is SHAKING.

cards.question: The Teacher sorts out where people's hearts are. True or false: he says the heart of the wise is in the house of pleasure.

cards.text: Then he puts two sounds side by side: a wise man's rebuke and the song of fools. One of those is a catchy tune, and the other one is your boss saying, “Got a minute? Close the door.”

cards.question: The Teacher says it is better to ___ a wise man's rebuke than to listen to the song of fools.

cards.text: Then he paints a picture you can hear: thorns going pop, pop, CRACKLE under a pot. Right after it, he adds one short line: “This too is futile.”

cards.question: The Teacher compares the crackling of thorns under the pot to something. What is it?

cards.text: Back to the Teacher's list, and now a warning about what can wreck even a wise man: extortion turns a wise man into a fool. Friend, if it can flip a WISE man, I'm keeping my mustache a long way from it.

cards.question: In the same verse as his warning about extortion, the Teacher says a bribe corrupts the heart. True or false?

cards.text: Then he says the end of a matter is better than the beginning. Friend, the beginning of a batch is flour in my mustache and dough on the ceiling, but the end is a sealed cookie box and me GLOWING.

cards.question: In that same line about endings and beginnings, the Teacher compares two kinds of spirit. Which one does he call better?
The Teacher says not to be quickly provoked in your spirit, for anger settles in the lap of a ___.

cards.text: Then he brings up a question people love to ask: “Why were the old days better than these?” Friend, I asked that one so many nights in the junk drawer, the dust started asking it WITH me.

cards.question: True or false: the Teacher says it is wise to ask why the old days were better than these.

cards.text: Then he says wisdom is good, like an inheritance, and it benefits those who see the sun. Friend, the only thing I ever inherited was a price sticker that said 25 cents.

cards.question: The Teacher says wisdom, like money, is a shelter, and wisdom preserves the ___ of its owner.

cards.text: Then the Teacher says to consider the work of God, and he asks a question about what God has bent. Friend, when it's God's work on the table, even I stop talking and LISTEN, and that's saying something.

cards.question: The Teacher asks who can ___ what God has bent.

cards.text: Last, he talks about two kinds of days: the day of prosperity and the day of adversity. Payday or flat tire, the man has a word for each one.

cards.question: What does the Teacher say to do in the day of prosperity?
In the day of adversity, the Teacher says to consider something. True or false: God has made the day of adversity along with the day of prosperity.
Why does the Teacher say God made the day of prosperity and the day of adversity together?

answers.text: So a man cannot discover what comes after him
So people learn to save up for hard times
So the proud are humbled and brought down low

findings.problem: The joke calls back to the 25-cent price sticker from the bin at the closing bakery. Nothing earlier in this lesson sets that up, and bakers only know about the junk drawer from onboarding, so the sticker line won't land.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: The core action of 7:11 is inheritance, meaning something good passed down to you. Nobody passed the price sticker down to him. It was stuck on him when he was for sale, so the comparison doesn't share the same action.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The joke adds a new backstory detail: that he asked 'Why were the old days better than these?' night after night in the junk drawer. The backstory doesn't include this, and it says he 'didn't talk much' in his drawer years. Jokes may invent small moments around his bakery, not new drawer history.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: Three of the walkthrough's jokes lean on the mustache: his mustache SHAKING (stop 1 card 5), keeping his mustache away from extortion (stop 2 card 1) and flour in his mustache (stop 2 card 3). That makes the mustache a recurring source of the humor.

rule.text: The mustache is a fact about him, not his main source of jokes.
